newsitem.title: USA: Dollar mixed at US noon, stg slide the focus.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mixed at US noon, stg slide the focus.

text.p: The dollar was mixed at midday after a decline in gold prices sent cross-rates gyrating, but the main focus was on the pound's across-the-board slide amid British business jitters about sterling's recent rise.

Cable commenced its nearly three-cent fall, triggering stop-loss selling at $1.6630 and $1.6600, as gold slid to 3-year lows. Sterling's fall gained speed amid talk of Bank of England sales, traders said.
"It's all premised on spot gold falling out of bed," said John Gariano, vice president at Sumitomo Bank. "That spilled over into some statements that sterling is too high."
The remarks added to the pound's woes by confirming that Britain will not be bound to the same ridgid fiscal discipline as countries seeking to join European Monetary Union in 1999.
Clarke reiterated Britain has no intention of joining the ERM.

Gold fell to its lowest level since November 1993, weakening the commodity-sensitive Australian dollar and sending Aussie/yen lower. There was also significant yen buying against the pound, which pummeled that cross.
After opening near at 73, mark/yen triggered stop-loss selling as it fell sharply below 72.80, traders said.

"There has been a fair amount of Aussie/yen selling and I think there has been in the last 48-hours enormous amounts of mark/yen selling -- a very technically negative situation having broken 73.40 (mark/yen)," said Stephen Jonathan, a director of foreign exchange at Merrill Lynch.
The surging yen also pushed dollar/yen below 114 in U.S. trade. Profit-takers with buy orders at 113.60 helped to slow the decline, dealers said.
"People become a bit self-correcting in dollar/yen as we aproach 115," Jonathan said. "The cross-move, because of what is happening in Europe, exacrbated it."
"There's a perception that the U.S. and Japan don't want the dollar to go above 115, so we're seeing dollar/yen liquidation," said Mike Malpede, a senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group Ltd.
Support for dollar/yen may have been dented early Tuesday after outgoing U.S. Ambassador to Japan, Walter Mondale said more work needs to be done to allow U.S. products into Japan.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.3280/90 Swiss francs from 1.3252/62 at the open and to Canadian $1.3483/88 from C$1.3472/77.
